ops.title: SMAppService.mainApp.status returns .notFound (not .notRegistered) until the first-ever register(); register() is the only reliable probe
ops.body:
Verified live on macOS 26 (Darwin 25.5.0) with CCPoolStatus.app v0.37.1: for a never-registered login item, `SMAppService.mainApp.status` returns `.notFound`, NOT `.notRegistered`. A switch that only registers from `.notRegistered` and treats `.notFound` as "dev build, retry later" silently never registers — no error, no log, no BTM entry (this shipped broken in cc-pool v0.37.1 and was fixed in v0.37.2 by attempting `register()` from every state except `.enabled`/`.requiresApproval`).

**Why:** Apple's docs imply .notFound is an error state, but for `mainApp` it is the normal pre-first-registration state. Status is not a reliable pre-flight check; only calling `register()` (and catching the throw) is.

**How to apply:** In `registerLoginItemOnce()`-style code, switch on `.enabled`/`.requiresApproval` → mark done; `default` → try `register()`. Verify registration empirically with `defaults read com.yasyf.cc-pool.status didRegisterLoginItem` and `sfltool dumpbtm | grep -A8 com.yasyf.cc-pool.status` (works unprivileged). Beware LaunchServices resolving `open -ga <name>` / bundle-ID launches to stray dev builds under `widget/build` — unregister with `lsregister -u` and delete the build products before testing.
